question_text: Containers of a particular brand of ice cream have a capacity of 1050 mL. They are advertised as containing 1 litre of ice cream. The quantity of ice cream added to each container is normally distributed with mean 1020 mL and standard deviation 17 mL.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that the container has less than the advertised capacity.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up normal distribution calculation $P(X \le 1000)$ with $\mu = 1020, \sigma = 17$

subparts.solution:
Let the capacity of a randomly selected container be $X\text{ mL}$.
$X \sim \text{N}(1020, 17^2)$.
Using technology:
Lower: $-9 \times 10^{99}$, Upper: $1000$, $\sigma = 17$, $\mu = 1020$
$$P(X \le 1000) \approx 0.120$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Standard normal cumulative calculation computes the area under the normal curve to the left of 1000.
step_by_step: Set up the lower bound as $-\infty$ (or $-9 \times 10^{99}$) and upper bound as $1000$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Entering variance $17^2 = 289$ instead of standard deviation $17$ into the calculator.

subparts.stem: Find the percentage of containers that overflow.
subparts.solution:
Using technology:
Lower: $1050$, Upper: $9 \times 10^{99}$, $\sigma = 17$, $\mu = 1020$
$$P(X \ge 1050) \approx 0.0388$$
$\therefore$ about $3.88\%$ of containers overflow.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The probability of an overflow corresponds to $P(X \ge 1050)$.
step_by_step: Set lower bound to $1050$ and upper bound to $\infty$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculating $P(X \le 1050)$ instead of the upper tail.

subparts.stem: A sample of 75 containers are taken. Find the probability that at most three of the containers overflow.
subparts.solution:
Let $Y$ be the number of containers which overflow.
$n = 75$, so $Y = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 75$ and $p \approx 0.0388$ {from b}
$\therefore Y \sim \text{B}(75, 0.0388)$
Using technology:
$$\text{BinomialCD}(0, 3, 75, 0.0388) \approx 0.667819$$
$$P(Y \le 3) \approx 0.668$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The number of overflowing containers in a sample of size $n$ follows a binomial distribution with success probability $p$ from part b.
step_by_step: Determine the probability of at most 3 overflowing: $P(Y \le 3)$.
Evaluate using binomial cumulative distribution on a GDC to get $0.668$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using normal approximation without checking conditions, or setting the upper bound to 2 instead of 3.
